title: Bug Fixing and Responsiveness
menuDescription: Bug fixes for application features, mobile layouts, and browser issues.
summary: Investigate broken features and layout problems, then check the fix against the affected behavior.

overview.title: Find out why a feature is failing.
paragraphs: We start by reproducing the bug. Then we trace it through the code and explain the fix before making changes.
Afterward, we check the affected feature and leave notes on the cause, the change, and any remaining issues.

features.title: Reproducible diagnosis
features.description: Clear steps, affected environments, and likely boundaries established before the fix.

features.title: Responsive layout repairs
features.description: Corrections for overflow, breakpoints, touch targets, and real-content edge cases.

features.title: Browser compatibility
features.description: Focused fixes for rendering and interaction differences across supported browsers.

features.title: Frontend debugging
features.description: State, event, rendering, and styling issues traced through the relevant components.

features.title: Integration debugging
features.description: Requests, responses, and interface contracts checked when issues cross system boundaries.

features.title: Regression checks
features.description: Check the affected feature and related behavior after the fix.

banner.title: Have a production issue your team cannot pin down?
banner.description: Send the page URL, the steps that trigger the issue, and a screenshot or error message.

faqs.question: What information helps you start debugging?
faqs.answer: A URL or environment, steps to reproduce, expected behavior, screenshots or logs, browser and device details, and the approximate time the issue began are all useful.

faqs.question: Do you need repository access?
faqs.answer: Many code-level issues require repository and environment access. We agree on the minimum access needed and work within the permissions your team provides.

faqs.question: Can you estimate a bug before investigating?
faqs.answer: We can estimate an initial diagnostic phase. A reliable fix estimate usually follows reproduction and root-cause analysis because similar symptoms can come from very different causes.

faqs.question: Can you debug a framework you did not originally build?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. We first review the stack, version, architecture, and available documentation to confirm that the issue is within our capability and safe to change.

faqs.question: Do you provide urgent production support?
faqs.answer: Availability depends on current commitments and the access required. Contact us with the impact and timing so we can confirm whether an expedited review is possible.
